chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Ziyād ibn Sūqah, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was asked about a man who deflowered his wife or his bondwoman, and she saw abundant blood that did not cease from her that day: how should she act regarding salat (prayer)?

He عليه السلام said: "She should insert cotton. If the cotton comes out ringed with blood, then it is from virginity; she performs ghusl (ritual bath), keeps a piece of cotton with her, and prays. But if the cotton comes out soaked in blood, then it is from menstruation; she refrains from salat (prayer) for the days of menstruation."

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: It is proper for her to refrain from salat (prayer), and this is among the matters over which there is no disagreement among the Muslims. This is also indicated by the first hadith in his statement, "Then let her leave the prayer," and their command denotes obligation.

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: Nor should she approach the mosque except passing through, and she should not touch the Qur'an nor any name among the Names of Allah the Exalted written on any thing. What has already passed in the chapter of janabah contains sufficient indication and proof for this, if Allah the Exalted wills.
Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: Fasting is not lawful for her. This too is among the matters upon which there is consensus, and that is also indicated by evidence.

key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: the menstrual period during which certain acts of worship are suspended
key_terms.الْعُذْرَةِ: virginity; here meaning bleeding caused by defloration
key_terms.الْكُرْسُفَ: cotton used here to determine the source of bleeding

ai.seo_question: How does a woman distinguish between bleeding from virginity and menstruation, and what are the rulings for prayer and fasting?
ai.summary: This hadith explains how to distinguish bleeding caused by loss of virginity from menstrual bleeding by means of cotton, and it sets out the legal consequences for salat (prayer). It also states related rulings for a menstruating woman, including refraining from prayer and fasting, not touching the Qur'an or the written Names of Allah, and not entering the mosque except in passing.
